reviewMethod: Fresh answerless browser-effective worksheet; prior authoring conclusions, tests, keys, rationales and prior audit claims treated as non-evidence. All 89 answers and verdicts completed before keyed reconciliation.

g8s-cr-001.value: Foam insulation performed best because its water remained at 63°C after 30 minutes, compared with 54°C for felt and 44°C with no insulation. Starting from 80°C, foam had the smallest temperature drop, so it minimized thermal-energy transfer most effectively.

g8s-cr-002.value: The unchanged 36.0 g total mass in the sealed container supports conservation of matter because no matter entered or left. The gas and new solid are new substances, but the atoms from the reactants are still present in the products; they were rearranged rather than created or destroyed.

g8s-cr-003.value: Greater food availability was associated with larger beetle populations: 17 beetles at 5 g/day, 30 at 10 g, 46 at 20 g, and 48 at 30 g. The increase from 20 to 30 g of food produced only 2 more beetles, so the response was not the same at every food level and another limiting factor may have become important.

g8s-cr-004.value: The data support an argument that the invasive plant may be affecting other wetland populations because native shoreline plant cover fell from 72% to 31% while insect species recorded fell from 18 to 11 under similar water depth. Additional repeated measurements from multiple comparable wetland sites, including sites without the invasive plant, would strengthen the causal argument.

g8s-cr-005.value: In one season, the bare 10 m bank lost 210 kg of sediment, the partly vegetated bank lost 122 kg, and the densely vegetated bank lost 55 kg, showing that vegetation is associated with less local erosion over a short time and small spatial scale. Repeated erosion and sediment transport across many bank sections over years can accumulate, consistent with the map evidence that the river channel shifted tens of meters over 25 years.

g8s-cr-006.value: Design A appears more effective: it reduced water use by 6,500 L/day, from 18,000 to 11,500 L/day, while Design B reduced use by 1,900 L/day, from 17,800 to 15,900 L/day. The town should continue monitoring factors such as rainfall, soil moisture, field use, or irrigation demand to confirm the difference persists under comparable conditions.
